judged_text: findMembers clamps offset against the possibly stale local user_count, so after member removals on later pages the client can request an offset within a shrunken range but the clamp uses the pre-refresh total. After removing members the refreshed count is fetched only via the response meta; in the window before refresh, next/previous navigation can compute offsets from a user_count that no longer matches the server, showing an empty page until the meta correction kicks in on the following fetch.

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group.findMembers` the requested `offset` is clamped using the client-side `user_count` (`Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)`), and the paging actions in `admin-group.js.es6` also bound offsets using `group.get("user_count")` before fetching (`next`: `Math.min(offset+limit, user_count)`). Since `user_count` is only refreshed from the server via the `findMembers()` response meta, it can be stale immediately after membership changes (e.g. removals) and allow requesting an offset that’s now beyond the server’s total, yielding an empty members list. The server endpoint (`GroupsController#members`) does not clamp the offset against `total` and simply applies `.offset(offset)`, so an out-of-range offset will return no members.
